title: Puerto Rico Governor Hosts First Diwali at Palace, Eyes India Trade Mission
excerpt: Jenniffer González-Colón hosted a Diwali celebration at Santa Catalina Palace on November 10 and, in an exclusive interview, linked India ties to pharma, aerospace and a possible trade mission next year.
body:
• Puerto Rico Governor Jenniffer González-Colón hosted a Diwali celebration at Santa Catalina Palace in San Juan on November 10 organised with PRDesi Cultural and Education Organization.
  • In an exclusive interview afterwards, she pointed to pharmaceuticals and medical devices — 45 percent of Puerto Rico's economy, she said — and sister plants in India as a direct link between the island and India.
  • She said a trade mission to India is something her administration will explore with its economic development department, possibly for next year.
  • She presented a proclamation to PRDesi founder Parveen Kaur Dhillon recognising the organisation's cultural and community work.

Puerto Rico Governor Jenniffer González-Colón hosted a Diwali celebration at Santa Catalina Palace, the governor's mansion in San Juan, on November 10 recognising the Indian American and broader South Asian community's contributions to the island. The gathering was organised with PRDesi Cultural and Education Organization (PRDesi CEO).

Following the Diwali dinner, González-Colón sat down for an exclusive interview with South Asian Herald that ended around midnight, discussing Puerto Rico's connections with India, opportunities in pharmaceuticals and aerospace, and the possibility of a trade mission to India.

A first Diwali at the palace

South Asian Herald described the evening as the first-ever Diwali celebration of its kind at the mansion.

At the celebration, González-Colón presented a proclamation to PRDesi CEO founder Parveen Kaur Dhillon and its board members, recognising the organisation's cultural and community work, South Asian Herald reported in its coverage of the event. The proclamation recognised PRDesi's commitment to education, cultural exchange and seva, the tradition of selfless service.

"PRDesi has distinguished itself in Puerto Rico through its dedication to sharing the cultural heritage of South Asia, fostering appreciation for its traditions, artistry, and enduring values."

— Jenniffer González-Colón, Governor of Puerto Rico

Dhillon recalled discussing Diwali with the governor over dinner more than a year earlier, after which González-Colón offered to host a celebration at her residence. Dhillon described the occasion as a milestone, saying the Indian community had grown considerably over the past five years.

The India link she described: pharma, devices and aerospace

"Many people are also unaware that pharmaceuticals and medical devices account for 45 percent of our economy. Manufacturing is a major part of Puerto Rico's economy, and India is a manufacturing hub as well. I believe that creates a direct connection," González-Colón told South Asian Herald.

Many pharmaceutical and medical device plants in Puerto Rico have sister facilities in India, she said, and engineers travel in both directions between those plants. Beyond those sectors, she pointed to aerospace work on the island at Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, Honeywell and other companies involved in aerospace and defense.

A possible trade mission, and the investment pitch

Asked about a trade delegation to India, she said: "That is something we will explore with our economic development department, possibly for next year. I believe it would be a valuable opportunity."

A trade mission could help attract companies interested in investing in Puerto Rico and taking advantage of available tax incentives, she said, noting that Japanese and Taiwanese companies are already investing because they want to manufacture in the United States, and that Indian companies could pursue similar opportunities using Puerto Rico as a hub to serve the Western Hemisphere. She also discussed Act 60 incentives, saying they require residency, investment or business operations on the island and have helped bring investment into infrastructure and housing while creating jobs.

Recovery and the grid

On recovery from Hurricane Maria, which struck in 2017, she said Puerto Rico had received more than $70 billion in investment for infrastructure, including telecommunications, water and electricity, and that rebuilding work using federal funding was still underway. Strengthening the electricity grid remained a priority, she said, adding that 1,900 megawatts of generation capacity had been added since last year and that public-private partnerships were being explored for more than 3,000 megawatts of new generation.

For South Asians considering Puerto Rico, her message in both the celebration and the interview was the same phrase repeated through the evening: Puerto Rico is open for business, and people who move there, invest there and create jobs are welcome.
